notes: Seeded from editor_config_template. One entry per option the export actually sets.

M3 repaired the importer's blind spot: the M0 pass registered an option only when one of the forms JetBrains *documents* for it appears in the template, so ~40 C#-relevant keys the export writes without a language prefix were dropped entirely and reported as SK9001 unknown keys. They are listed in UNDOCUMENTED_CSHARP_KEYS in tools/import-options.py now, and carry since = 0.4 here.

defaultSource: `resharper-docs` means JetBrains' published tables state the default (they do not, for any key — the tables document names, languages and possible values only). `oracle-probe` means the default was derived by running `jb cleanupcode` under a configuration carrying nothing but `root = true` and comparing the result with the fixture that exercises the option (docs/plan/03 § "Deriving ReSharper's defaults"). `template` means the recorded value is the export's own, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two.
`skala config distill` drops a key only when defaultSource is resharper-docs or oracle-probe and the value equals the default.
Tier A is claimed only where the formatter reads the option AND a committed oracle fixture pins it.

options.summary: The file's character encoding. The EditorConfig specification enumerates the domain: “Set to latin1, utf-8, utf-8-bom, utf-16be or utf-16le to control the character set.” ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against `jb cleanupcode` 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended `[*.cs]` section — the sweep's own method — and classified not a formatter option. Probed at `utf-8`, `utf-8-bom`, `latin1` and `utf-16le` on a file carrying non-ASCII text, comparing raw bytes rather than normalised text: the oracle returned the same bytes at all four, adding no BOM and re-encoding nothing, and so did Skala. Neither engine re-encodes, so no oracle fixture can pin this key.

Indent the braces of a block themselves. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-30 against `jb cleanupcode` 2025.2.6: it governs a brace that is on a LINE OF ITS OWN, and the oracle is flat at both values under the export's `csharp_new_line_before_open_brace = none`. With the braces split (`= all`) the answer is Whitesmiths — the brace takes one level and the body takes the SAME level: `class C` / `    {` / `    void M()` / `        {` / `        if (true)`. Skala applied it whatever the brace placement, so under `none` the joined opening brace could not move and the closing one did, producing a shape no configuration of either key writes. SK-DIV-0091.
options.inert: Masked by `csharp_new_line_before_open_brace = none` in the export: it indents a brace that is on its own line and this configuration never puts one there, so no input distinguishes its values — the oracle is flat at both too. ⚠ Not unimplemented: `BracePlacementTests` pins the Whitesmiths shape it produces once the braces are split. ⚠ Its sweep row reads INERT rather than UNEXERCISED, and that is the probe: the sweep appends the key in an `[*.cs]` section of its own, and ReSharper re-derives the Roslyn brace pair from that section — defaulting the absent `csharp_new_line_before_open_brace` to Roslyn's `all` — so the oracle answers a question about brace PLACEMENT that was never asked. Supply both keys in the same section and the oracle is flat at both values, which is what Skala reproduces. SK-DIV-0091.

options.summary: Put each member of an object initializer on its own line. ⚠ Observable, and masked rather than inert: this export sets `place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = true`, which joins a short initializer whatever this key says. Lift that and it answers — and it answers with the polarity reversed and over two targets at once. At `false` the oracle writes `new Thing { A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 }` even under `place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = false` AND `wrap_object_and_collection_initializer_style = chop_always`, so `false` here overrides both. ⚠ Blocked on the one mechanism the registry does not have: `expands` propagates a generalized key's value TEXT into the keys it names, so it can only reach targets whose domain — and whose polarity — is its own. Three keys need the same missing piece and none of them is a coverage gap: this one, `csharp_space_between_parentheses` and `csharp_new_line_before_members_in_object_initializers`. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against `jb cleanupcode` 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended `[*.cs]` section — the sweep's own method — and classified masked. The recorded mask is confirmed: at the export's `resharper_place_simple_initializer_on_single_line = true` both engines are flat; lift it and the oracle produces two distinct outputs while Skala stays flat, so a single-key `oracle` glob would report INERT. ⚠ The unprefixed spelling IS read by the C# formatter — the blanket claim near PhaseOneOptions.cs ~1279 does not hold for this key.

Which constructs put '{' on a new line. Microsoft documents `all`, `none`, or one or more of twelve code elements separated by commas. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-30 against `jb cleanupcode` 2025.2.6, one value per run, on a probe whose every body holds two statements and every initializer six elements so that no `place_simple_*` rule could join a construct and hide the brace: the C# formatter answers to SEVEN of the twelve, and the other five are covered by a neighbour and move nothing on their own. `types` also takes a block NAMESPACE; `methods` also takes LOCAL FUNCTIONS; `properties` takes the accessor LIST of a property, an indexer and an event alike; `accessors` takes the accessor BODY; `lambdas` also takes an anonymous method's `delegate(…) { }`; `object_collection_array_initializers` also takes a SWITCH EXPRESSION's and a PROPERTY PATTERN's braces. Inert: `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `events`, `indexers`, `local_functions`. `all` is exactly the union of the seven, confirmed rather than assumed. ⚠ Skala read this flags option as a two-valued switch — every value but `none` behaved as `all`, and 2 of its 15 values agreed with the oracle; now 15 of 15. ⚠ The SPLIT direction is not implemented: brace placement here is a join decision, so a K&R input under a non-`none` value comes back K&R where the oracle splits. Invisible to this row, whose fixture is written Allman. SK-DIV-0091.
Put each LINQ query clause on its own line.

IDE0011 documents `true`, `false` and `when_multiline`. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against `jb cleanupcode` 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended `[*.cs]` section — the sweep's own method — and classified wrong subsystem — a Roslyn analyser's.
